attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The nontrivial missing proof is not convex closedness itself; it is the domination claim \(\tau_{RG}\succeq\tau_{OS}^{\mathrm{quad}}\) for the actual Balaban-style compactness topology, especially for reflected products that approach the time-zero plane and for renormalized composite gauge-invariant observables.
steps: Fix \(F_1,\dots,F_N\in\mathcal A_+^{\mathrm{gi}}\) and \(c\in\mathbb C^N\). At each cutoff define \(Q_{a,L}(F,c)=\sum_{i,j}\overline c_i c_j S_{a,L}((\Theta F_i)F_j)\).
Use regulated reflection positivity to obtain \(Q_{a,L}(F,c)\ge0\) for every cutoff in the net.
Assume \(S_{a,L}\to S\) in \(\tau_{RG}\) and that \(\tau_{RG}\) dominates the finite reflected-form topology. Then \(Q_{a,L}(F,c)\to Q_S(F,c)\).
Since the closed half-line \([0,\infty)\subset\mathbb R\) is closed, the limit satisfies \(Q_S(F,c)\ge0\). This proves continuum reflection positivity for the fixed finite family.

Quantify over all finite families in the locked positive-time algebra. The OS inner product \(S((\Theta F)G)\) is therefore positive semidefinite and has a valid null quotient completion, provided the other OS axioms are available.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The argument is conditionally valid as functional analysis, but it has not shown that the Yang-Mills RG estimates give continuity of every reflected quadratic probe on one cutoff-independent observable algebra. It also has not established Euclidean covariance, clustering, regularity, or the mass gap; it only preserves the OS-positivity invariant if the topology and same-theory locking obligations are met.

assumptions: For every finite \(F_1,\dots,F_N\in\mathcal A_+^{\mathrm{gi}}\) and coefficients \(c\in\mathbb C^N\), the map \(S\mapsto Q_S(F,c)\) is \(\tau_{RG}\)-continuous.
Each regulated functional is reflection positive: \(Q_{S_{a,L}}(F,c)\ge0\) for all finite reflected tests.
The continuum candidate \(S\) is the same \(\tau_{RG}\)-limit used to prove the distributional Schwinger functions, not a separately extracted OS-positive subsequential limit.
Products \((\Theta F_i)F_j\) remain in the distributional domain controlled by the multiscale estimates.
definitions: source object: a net \(S_{a,L}\) of regulated gauge-invariant Euclidean Schwinger functionals on one fixed algebra \(\mathcal A^{\mathrm{gi}}\), each satisfying finite reflection-positivity inequalities on \(\mathcal A_+^{\mathrm{gi}}\).

target object: continuum OS-positive Schwinger functions \(S\) on \(\mathcal A^{\mathrm{gi}}\), suitable for OS reconstruction of a physical Hilbert space after the remaining OS axioms are separately verified.
controlled interface: regulated reflection-positive Schwinger forms -> OS-positive continuum Schwinger functions, mediated only by convergence of reflected finite quadratic forms.

same-theory condition: the reflected test algebra, reflection map, renormalized observable labels, and gauge-invariant quotient are independent of \((a,L)\); no change of theory is hidden in gauge fixing, completion, or counterterm-dependent observable redefinition.

equations.valid_when: \(F_i\in\mathcal A_+^{\mathrm{gi}}\), \(c_i\in\mathbb C\), and the product observable is in the common gauge-invariant test domain.

equations.label: cone closure
equations.valid_when: The convergence is along the same cutoff-removal net and each finite reflected quadratic form is continuous in the chosen topology.

equations.label: OS null-space inner product
equations.valid_when: The preceding closure has made the sesquilinear form positive semidefinite on the continuum positive-time algebra.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A falsifier is any pair \((F,c)\) for which \(S_{a,L}\to S\) in the advertised multiscale topology but \(Q_{S_{a,L}}(F,c)\not\to Q_S(F,c)\), or for which \((\Theta F_i)F_j\) leaves the controlled observable domain.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This lemma isolates the minimum topological bridge needed for invariant preservation: OS positivity need not be reconstructed by hand if the RG topology already sees every reflected quadratic probe.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Let \(\mathcal A_+^{\mathrm{gi}}\) be a cutoff-independent positive-time gauge-invariant test algebra with reflection \(\Theta\). If the RG cutoff-removal topology \(\tau_{RG}\) on Schwinger functionals is at least as strong as the initial topology generated by all finite reflected quadratic forms \(S\mapsto \sum_{i,j}\overline c_i c_j S((\Theta F_i)F_j)\), then every \(\tau_{RG}\)-limit of regulated reflection-positive Schwinger functionals is OS reflection positive on \(\mathcal A_+^{\mathrm{gi}}\).

assumptions: The renormalization of composite gauge-invariant observables is triangular and reflection-covariant.
Reflection-plane counterterms are absent or have been included in the fixed observable definition with a proven positive limit.
The limiting topology controls coincident-time singularities created by multiplying reflected positive-time observables.
definitions: Continuum tests are not arbitrary gauge fields; they are gauge-invariant smeared Wilson loops, curvature polynomials after gauge-invariant smearing, or other chosen cylinder observables supported in positive Euclidean time.

The locking map must preserve positive-time support with a uniform buffer away from the reflection hyperplane, or else reflection can create contact terms not controlled by ordinary distributional convergence.
Product compatibility means the regulator-level observable assigned to \((\Theta F)G\) has the same limit as \((\Theta\iota_{a,L}F)(\iota_{a,L}G)\).

equations.label: reflection covariance of embeddings
equations.valid_when: The regulator reflection and continuum reflection are compared on the same locked gauge-invariant algebra.

equations.label: multiplicative locking
equations.valid_when: Composite observable renormalization is compatible with reflected products in the chosen cutoff-removal topology.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A concrete falsifier would be a required wave-function or composite renormalization mixing matrix that is not reflection-covariant, so that a valid lattice-positive quadratic form converges to the wrong continuum quadratic form.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This lemma names the hidden same-theory obligation behind the closed-cone argument; without it, positivity may pass to a different algebra than the one used for the continuum Yang-Mills claim.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Reflection positivity can be transported through cutoff removal only after the positive-time gauge-invariant observables are locked across scales by a single embedding \(\iota_{a,L}:\mathcal A_+^{\mathrm{gi,cont}}\to\mathcal A_{+,a,L}^{\mathrm{gi}}\) satisfying \(\Theta\iota_{a,L}(F)=\iota_{a,L}(\Theta F)\) and product compatibility up to errors vanishing in the reflected quadratic topology.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot if Balaban-style bounds only give convergence for separated ordinary Schwinger distributions and cannot be strengthened to reflected products or time-zero contact terms without changing the observable algebra.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote if a named \(\tau_{RG}\) is proved to dominate \(\tau_{OS}^{\mathrm{quad}}\) on a fixed reflection-covariant gauge-invariant algebra, with explicit estimates for composite reflected products.
control_decision.reason: The branch remains productive because it converted repeated vocabulary into a falsifiable topology-domination lemma and a separate same-theory locking lemma.

dependency_updates.description: Reduced the bridge to a domination requirement between the RG cutoff-removal topology and the initial topology generated by finite reflected OS quadratic probes.
The algebra must be cutoff-independent, positive-time stable, reflection-covariant, and closed under reflected products after renormalized observable locking.
The candidate topology must control not merely distributional correlators but the scalar evaluations of all products \((\Theta F_i)F_j\), including near-reflection-plane contact behavior.

falsifiers: Topology falsifier: construct a sequence of regulated Schwinger functionals converging in the multiscale distribution topology while a reflected quadratic form has a negative or nonconvergent continuum value.

Algebra falsifier: show that the gauge-invariant positive-time algebra used at cutoff depends on \((a,L)\) through renormalization choices so no single \(\mathcal A_+^{\mathrm{gi}}\) receives all positivity inequalities.
Reflection-plane falsifier: find a contact counterterm supported at \(t=0\) that is invisible to separated-time RG bounds but changes \(S((\Theta F)F)\).

Gauge-quotient falsifier: demonstrate that positivity holds before imposing the continuum Gauss-law or gauge-invariant quotient but fails after the quotient/completion used for the claimed physical theory.

Subsequence falsifier: the only OS-positive continuum object is obtained by an extraction different from the one yielding the claimed Schwinger distributions, so the bridge does not preserve the same theory.
branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: The real bridge lemma is almost tautological once the right topology is named: reflection-positive functionals form a closed convex cone in the initial topology of finite OS quadratic forms. The discovery pressure has therefore moved to two precise obligations: prove the RG compactness topology is valid for those reflected probes, and prove the locked gauge-invariant observable algebra is the same theory before and after cutoff removal. This separates a formal closed-cone preservation step from the substantive Yang-Mills analytic estimate still missing.
branch_outputs.next_experiment: Work on one representative family, such as smeared small Wilson-loop curvature observables supported in \(t>\epsilon\), and test whether the multiscale bounds imply convergence of \(S_{a,L}((\Theta F_i)F_j)\) uniformly as \(a\to0,L\to\infty\); then decrease \(epsilon\) toward the reflection plane to expose the first contact-term obstruction.
